aiNative.role: canonical findings, backlog, implementation, and verification

digests.dateEvidence: No explicit issue date in source output

findings.title: Active-SWE: coding agents still struggle when nobody tells them exactly what the bug is.
findings.practicalTakeaway: Make problem discovery a gated phase: supply logs, failing tests, telemetry, issue history, and repository context; require diagnosis and evidence before implementation.

findings.title: Self-evolving coding agents are becoming a distinct engineering pattern.
findings.practicalTakeaway: Persist verified lessons rather than generic chat memory; promote human corrections into versioned instructions, skills, executable checks, or retrieval sources.

findings.title: Coding agents increase completion speed while potentially reducing developer understanding.
findings.practicalTakeaway: Use human gates to test understanding and judgment; have the agent summarize architectural impact, decisions, assumptions, risks, and evidence for explicit approval.

findings.title: Agent-generated tests may be broader but less trustworthy operationally.
findings.practicalTakeaway: Separate implementation from verification; define or approve requirements-derived tests before implementation and check flakiness, mutation strength, and assertion quality.

findings.title: Repository knowledge is shifting from static documentation toward living engineering context.
findings.practicalTakeaway: Treat vectors as one retrieval mechanism alongside repository graphs, git history, tickets, tests, logs, and explicit instructions; route by question.

findings.title: Warp is explicitly productizing the “software factory” model
findings.practicalTakeaway: Keep development agent-agnostic; define requirements, lifecycle stages, evidence, and human gates outside the executor.

findings.title: Slack Code pushes agentic development into a shared human/agent workspace
findings.practicalTakeaway: Preserve the agent trajectory as an engineering artifact: requirements, decisions, tests, failures, evidence, and approvals.

findings.title: “Auditable agents” gives human-in-the-loop a better technical definition
findings.practicalTakeaway: Capture input, assumption, action, evidence, and decision for every lifecycle phase.

findings.title: The “humans cannot review all generated code” argument is getting sharper
findings.practicalTakeaway: Center TDD on evidence produced before and during implementation: requirements-derived tests, static checks, mutation tests, runtime assertions, and targeted judgment.

findings.title: MAGE: turn engineering judgment into durable constraints, not repeated prompts
findings.practicalTakeaway: Classify knowledge along context→guidance→invariant→acceptance criterion→enforced gate; promote security boundaries and definition-of-done items to executable controls and evidence.

findings.title: Formal verification is becoming surprisingly practical when agents do the proof work
findings.practicalTakeaway: Move verification toward independently computable mechanisms such as properties, mutation testing, schemas, static analysis, contracts, and invariants.

findings.title: Goldman is turning “tribal knowledge” into reusable agent skills
findings.practicalTakeaway: Promote repeated corrections through conversation correction→documented rule→reusable skill→automated check.

findings.title: Security research is arguing for an “assurance case,” not a passing test suite
findings.practicalTakeaway: Require each phase to emit an evidence bundle covering requirements, tests, static/security checks, assumptions, unresolved uncertainty, and required human decisions.

findings.title: Harness-of-Harness: sustained agent work improves when the outer loop controls progress
findings.practicalTakeaway: Make each orchestrated phase small, independently verifiable, and outcome-constrained; allow eager execution inside it and do not accept the implementer’s own tests as final evidence.

findings.title: WiseSpec quantifies how much better requirements can improve agent performance
findings.practicalTakeaway: Expand phase contracts to goal→constraints/unknowns→acceptance evidence→definition of done→execute; force ambiguity challenge before implementation.

findings.title: GitHub has useful production evidence that optimizing token counts can actually make agents worse
findings.practicalTakeaway: Treat agent configuration as executable software and add behavioral evals/regression tests for instructions, skills, tools, and MCP configuration.

findings.title: FrontierSWE v2 moves evaluation toward the kind of work where agents actually need engineering endurance
findings.practicalTakeaway: Evaluate at least one multi-hour realistic task; measure human redirections, discarded work, and whether final evidence supports completion.

findings.title: Gartner formally identifies Coding Agent Harness Engineering as an emerging discipline
findings.practicalTakeaway: Keep models interchangeable; store requirements, lifecycle, evidence, and authority outside the executor.

findings.title: A source-code study finds production coding agents aren't actually using vector RAG for code
findings.practicalTakeaway: Separate organizational knowledge retrieval from deterministic code navigation; use embeddings for docs/history and search, symbols, git, and tools for code.

findings.title: The strongest harness results suggest the system can learn, not just the model
findings.practicalTakeaway: Convert interventions into the most durable suitable control: instruction, skill, tool, validator, test, or workflow constraint.

findings.title: A new industry survey exposes a governance gap around agents
findings.practicalTakeaway: Maintain separate product-verification and agent-verification suites.

findings.title: Andrew Ng's new workflow puts the human precisely where verification stops being objective
findings.practicalTakeaway: Retain human checkpoints only where humans make judgment that cannot yet be reliably automated.

findings.title: AgentGuard turns previous agent failures into conditional guardrails
findings.practicalTakeaway: Add a failure-promotion loop: intervention→classify cause→generalizable guardrail→regression scenario; do not promote every correction.

findings.title: We now have evidence that the agent harness itself is becoming a software supply chain
findings.practicalTakeaway: Treat agent configuration as a supply chain: pin MCP versions, review skills, enumerate permissions, code-review configuration, and scan it in CI.

findings.title: RAG research shows why retrieving knowledge about failures can beat retrieving similar code
findings.practicalTakeaway: Split engineering retrieval by intent: code navigation, architecture, precedent, failure knowledge, and policy.

findings.title: 1Password published unusually concrete production numbers for agent-assisted delivery
findings.practicalTakeaway: Measure AI rollout with delivery outcomes—cycle time, escaped defects, rework, failed changes, MTTR, and human intervention—not usage, tokens, or LOC.

findings.title: Anthropic's internal usage provides a useful reality check on “autonomy”
findings.practicalTakeaway: Track AI participation separately from where and why human judgment was required.

findings.title: Agent regression testing may have just become dramatically cheaper
findings.practicalTakeaway: Retain representative trajectories and use behaviorally representative subsets for harness CI; compare completion, violations, and human interventions after changes.

findings.title: Self-improving harnesses have acquired the same overfitting problem as ML models
findings.practicalTakeaway: Before promoting an intervention into a permanent rule, distinguish engineering invariant from incident-specific answer and regression-test it on unrelated tasks.

findings.title: GPT-6 Astra materially raises the ceiling — but its design reinforces judgment-based HITL
findings.practicalTakeaway: Define human gates by decision type: proceed on reversible/verifiable work; record low-consequence assumptions; ask on architecture, security, or product judgment; require approval for irreversible/high-impact actions.

findings.title: Engineering RAG: retrieval quality can matter more than model size
findings.practicalTakeaway: Prototype engineering knowledge with AST/symbol graphs, dependencies, generated architecture summaries, embeddings, and git/work-item/incident retrieval.

findings.title: Merged agent PRs need significantly more follow-up fixing than human PRs
findings.practicalTakeaway: Add 30/60-day post-merge quality metrics for rework, regressions, follow-up fixes, and escaped defects; optimize for production-qualified change.

findings.title: Meta's verification work makes an intriguing proposal: review the specification instead of all the generated code
findings.practicalTakeaway: Have an independent agent derive a behavioral contract after implementation; review that contract plus tests/evidence instead of relying only on line-by-line review.

findings.title: “Green doesn't mean done” applies even to formal proofs
findings.practicalTakeaway: Move human checkpoints upstream: humans own or approve what must be true, machines implement/prove it, and humans decide unresolved judgment or exceptions.

findings.title: Long-horizon agent memory may not require a fancy memory subsystem at all
findings.practicalTakeaway: Use simple, inspectable repository-local working-memory artifacts—plans, decisions, assumptions, evidence, and open questions—with git history and provenance.

findings.title: Token efficiency is becoming an explicit agent optimization target
findings.practicalTakeaway: Evaluate verified outcome per total execution cost, including tokens, CI runs, elapsed time, discarded work, and human intervention.

findings.title: SWE-CC: Coding agents violate 43% of applicable repository policies
findings.practicalTakeaway: Separate product verification from process verification and convert important repository policies into deterministic checks.

findings.title: Teaching Agents to Code Reliably: Better verification beats additional attempts
findings.practicalTakeaway: Enforce a boundary between implementation and acceptance; require evidence against pre-established requirements, independent of self-authored tests.

findings.title: GitHub's ReviewBench gives AI code review a more meaningful benchmark
findings.practicalTakeaway: Evaluate AI reviewers on defect detection, false-positive rate, and human review effort.

findings.title: GitLab's governed software factory brings engineering RAG into the SDLC
findings.practicalTakeaway: Provide unified engineering retrieval across code, git history, work items, CI results, operational telemetry, and decisions.

findings.title: Microsoft demonstrates reinforcement learning directly against real coding-agent harnesses
findings.practicalTakeaway: Preserve structured trajectories—tasks, tool calls, context, failures, interventions, verification, and outcomes—for future evals, harness improvement, or training.

findings.title: Doc2Harness: We can now benchmark the engineering system around an agent
findings.practicalTakeaway: Build a deterministic behavioral regression suite for permissions, tool execution, state persistence, error recovery, and approval gates using scripted model responses.

findings.title: Interaction-as-a-Judge: Testing the UI like a human beats inspecting code
findings.practicalTakeaway: Pair deterministic UI tests with an independent interaction agent that exercises user-facing acceptance criteria.

findings.title: StateHarness: Persistent project knowledge improves long-running coding agents
findings.practicalTakeaway: Separate project knowledge, working state, and historical knowledge; keep important working state inspectable and versioned.

findings.title: Tangent: Most agent testing is still surprisingly shallow
findings.practicalTakeaway: Add fault-injection tests for tool failures, malformed responses, permission denials, interruptions, stale context, and failed recovery; assess constraint-safe recovery.

findings.title: REAG: RAG can generate better acceptance tests, not just better answers
findings.practicalTakeaway: Use a separate acceptance-verification agent grounded in approved requirements, decisions, and policies; it must abstain or escalate when evidence is insufficient.

findings.title: REM: Coding agents improve when memory is selective and temporary
findings.practicalTakeaway: Separate durable organizational knowledge from temporary task experience; retrieve prior failures and solutions only when relevant.

findings.title: Skip the Compressor: Whole source files outperform compressed context
findings.practicalTakeaway: Use deterministic search and dependency relationships to identify candidate code, then provide complete source files instead of compressed fragments when budget permits.

findings.title: Agentic Verified Optimization: Agents can optimize software and prove equivalence
findings.practicalTakeaway: For performance refactors, use independently owned behavioral contracts and property-based tests.

findings.title: Automated migration testing exposes the limits of verification gates
findings.practicalTakeaway: Inject deliberate defects or mutations to measure whether AI-generated acceptance tests detect meaningful failures.

findings.title: AI-assisted development isn't necessarily producing more homogeneous or lower-quality code
findings.practicalTakeaway: Evaluate AI adoption with maintainability, defect density, rework, change-failure rate, and delivery speed—not code volume.

findings.title: Independent agent review delivers measurable gains at modest cost
findings.practicalTakeaway: Add a read-only independent reviewer given approved requirements, diff, and test evidence; reserve humans for disputed requirements, architecture, and unresolved risk.

findings.title: Rivet shows why engineering RAG needs dependency-aware context
findings.practicalTakeaway: Prioritize evidence completeness over semantic similarity: retrieve implementation, callers, dependencies, tests, and configuration constraints before broader documentation.

findings.title: InfraDev reveals how often passing tests conceal incorrect infrastructure changes
findings.practicalTakeaway: Verify latency, memory, concurrency, recovery, and operational constraints in addition to unit and mutation results; define these criteria before implementation.

findings.title: GitHub Copilot Fusion makes multi-model orchestration a mainstream IDE feature
findings.practicalTakeaway: Keep the lifecycle model-independent and benchmark task completion, verified quality, total cost, and human-intervention time.

findings.title: Instant Software Factories exposes a dangerous productivity measurement trap
findings.practicalTakeaway: Measure independently validated, production-qualified changes—not commits, merges, or issues—and keep acceptance criteria plus critical CI outside unrestricted agent authority.

findings.title: Agent skills are evolving faster than their reliability practices
findings.practicalTakeaway: Give every important skill an execution contract—prerequisites, allowed actions, evidence, recovery, and completion—and regression-test it on representative tasks.

findings.title: GenDB-V demonstrates the power of fixed specifications and independent proof
findings.practicalTakeaway: Freeze acceptance contracts before implementation; agents may optimize within them but cannot weaken or rewrite success criteria.

findings.title: Agent memory needs dependency tracking, not just retrieval
findings.practicalTakeaway: Attach source, date, repository version, and dependencies to retrieved knowledge; revalidate downstream decisions and runbooks when upstream assumptions change.

findings.title: OpenAI demonstrates a large-scale discover → reproduce → patch → review pipeline
findings.practicalTakeaway: Use a discover→reproduce→patch→regression-validate pipeline with independent analysis and human approval for consequential changes.

findings.title: Launder-Bench reveals a new software provenance problem
findings.practicalTakeaway: Preserve licenses, source references, and derivation decisions whenever agents consult external repositories.
